articles.title: Martin McDonagh says CIA has ‘done awful things all around the world’
articles.summary: McDonagh’s new film, Wild Horse Nine, stars John Malkovich as an agent in 1970s Chile who feels ‘guilt and regret’ over his role in global interventions. The US’s history of intervening in democratic processes around the world deserves more attention in the light of current political developments…
body: “I’ve been very interested in the truth of what the CIA has been doing over the last 60 years, and the awful things they’ve done all around the world,” McDonagh said about Wild Horse Nine, his first film since his 2022 tragicomedy The Banshees of Inisherin. “I think maybe something that’s not talked about enough. We know what the KGB are like, but we probably don’t question the CIA’s activity as much as we ought to.”

In Wild Horse Nine, John Malkovich plays Chris, a veteran agent for the foreign intelligence service who is stationed in Santiago, Chile, on the eve of the US-supported coup against Salvador Allende – Latin America’s first democratically elected Marxist president – in 1973. Recently diagnosed with cancer and acting erratically, Chris is dispatched to Easter Island with his protege Lee (Sam Rockwell), where he starts to reflect critically on his role in other CIA interventions, including the Guatemalan coup d’état of 1954, the 1961 assassination of revolutionary Congolese prime minister Patrice Lumumba and – according to the film’s telling – the killing of John F Kennedy.

articles.title: Tall tales: the 20 best giants in film – ranked!
articles.summary: On the 300th anniversary of Gulliver’s Travels, we celebrate the biggest film stars of them all – from a stone colossus to a metal-munching alien and a 50ft woman on the rampage.
body: Not a first-person-shooter BFG, alas, but one of Steven Spielberg’s worst films, reducing Roald Dahl’s story to digital pap. Mo-cap Mark Rylance, whose cutesy ungrammatical babbling should have been left on the printed page, is the 24ft Big Friendly Giant who kidnaps an orphan girl, Sophie. Ugh. Big Creepy Giant, more like.

Nicholas Hoult plays the farmhand who forms an implausible alliance with a princess in a fairytale cluttered with extraneous characters. Bill Nighy plays half of a two-headed giant, but the actors are swamped by digital effects and anti-giant propaganda. The best bit is when a massive chef rolls an extraneous Ewan McGregor in pastry and puts him in an oven.

“Stone giants!” JRR Tolkien seemingly preferred dwarves to the big people, but Peter Jackson’s three-part rendering of his stand-alone children’s classic is briefly enlivened by stone colossuses hurling boulders at each other in a thunderstorm. Though one can’t help thinking how awesome a Ray Harryhausen version might have been.
points: On the 300th anniversary of Gulliver’s Travels, we celebrate the biggest film stars of them all – from a stone colossus to a metal-munching alien and a 50ft woman on the rampage.

articles.title: Oscar-Nominated Animator Theodore Ushev to Present Adaptation of Shane Jones’ Cult Novel ‘Light Boxes’ in Venice
articles.summary: Bulgarian filmmaker Theodore Ushev, Oscar-nominated in the animated short film category in 2017 for “Blind Vaysha,” is in pre-production on feature film “Light Boxes,” which he will present at the Venice Production Bridge’s Gap-Financing Market, running Sept. 4-6.
body: Seeking refuge from constant bombardment, Anna discovers Bianca, her imaginary double, living in a fantastical town imprisoned by a war of its own. There, the tyrannical February has condemned its inhabitants to eternal winter and forbids them from flying, while a masked resistance movement known as The Solution fights to restore light and freedom.
With neither reality nor imagination offering an escape from tyranny, the film asks whether hope, memory and love can persevere when war threatens to extinguish them all.

For Ushev, survival lies in imitation. “The characters are constantly trying to reproduce what they have lost to convince themselves it can somehow return,” he tells Variety. “That is what I find fascinating about every totalitarian regime – no matter how oppressed people become, they will always find ways to recreate what has been taken from them, to keep hope alive.”

articles.title: Camilo Séptimo Keyboardist Jonathan Meléndez, His Pregnant Wife and 3-Year Old Daughter Murdered in Mexico
articles.summary: Jonathan Meléndez, keyboardist for the Mexican group Camilo Séptimo, his wife, 3-year-old daughter, and nanny were found murdered at their home near Mexico City, according to a statement from the State of Mexico Prosecutor’s Office and CNN.
body: Two men have been arrested in connection with the murders, according to a statement from Omar García Harfuch, the country’s secretary of public security. He said one of the suspects, partially identified by authorities as Diego Sebastián “N,” was a business partner of a victim and “allegedly used that relationship of trust to gain access to the residence.”
“Today we honor and celebrate his life, his music, his light, and what he shared with those of us fortunate enough to know him and walk alongside him,” Camilo Séptimo wrote in social media posts.

Camilo Séptimo was formed in Mexico City in 2013 by Meléndez (pictured above, right) singer Manuel Mendoza and guitarist Erik Vázquez. The band released an EP in 2014 and its first album, “Óleos” (“oil paintings”) in 2017, which reached No. 10 on the Mexican albums charts. The group followed with three more albums, the most recent being 2023’s “Jardín de las almas” (“garden of souls”).

articles.title: ‘Bucking Fastard’ Review: Herner Werzog’s Uddled-Mup Fairytale Stars the Mara Sisters as You’ve Never Seen Her Before
articles.summary: Occasionally sublime, often ridiculous and always extravagantly weird, Werner Herzog’s “Bucking Fastard,” unlike its gorgeously interlinked protagonists, is a film of multiple personalities that only rarely speak in unison.
body: Kate and Rooney Mara give a single, intricately virtuosic performance speaking and acting in perfect concert that cannot quite unify the great German eccentric's cluttered, ripely bonkers fantasia.

It feels almost heretical to wish that a Werner Herzog film were just a little less outlandish. But while “Bucking Fastard” gives us, in the Mara sisters’ uncannily synced-up performances, a novelty worth the price of admission alone, it is mired in so much mythology and mystery that by the end, the fact of the sisters being two who respond and react as one becomes all but immaterial. If anything, perhaps it’s born of fondness: Herzog has amassed a rogues’ gallery of freaks and madmen and outcasts in his back catalogue, but seldom has he dealt with any of them this kindly, this sweetly and with this little hard-edged insight into why they behave the way that they do.

articles.title: Star Trek IV: The Voyage Home review – Kirk, Spock and co on semi-intentionally hilarious save-the-whale mission
articles.summary: Our heroes travel back through time to San Francisco in 1986 so they can commune with aliens threatening future Earth – it’s preposterously good fun. Here is the fourth and silliest movie in the Star Trek franchise, now on rerelease for its 40th anniversary.
body: Spock has been brought back to life, as the apparent end result of all the bizarre metempsychotic plot contortions of the previous film. But the permanent and irrevocable death of Kirk’s son seems to be passed over remarkably casually. The eerie boyishness of Shatner’s Kirk, with that beaming smile, almost makes you forget that he has been through an agonising bereavement. Hasn’t he?
points: Our heroes travel back through time to San Francisco in 1986 so they can commune with aliens threatening future Earth – it’s preposterously good fun.

articles.title: Falling House review – fierce tale of an Iranian prison guard holding his family hostage
articles.summary: Venice film festival: Mohsen Gharaei’s powerfully acted domestic drama watches as the failing patriarch attempts to contain family rebellion. Iran is a prison and everybody is inside: cons and non-cons; parents and their children.
body: Gharaei’s previous picture, Without Everything, was a major box office hit in Iran in 2021, and was lavished with awards at the Fajr film festival in Tehran. This one looks set for a rather rockier reception, assuming it is permitted to land safely at all. It’s an angry, cornered beast of a movie, a rugged piece of old-school social realism and a thinly veiled parable of life in the Islamic Republic. Escape, it suggests, is the only reasonable option. But for that one needs money, a passport and a key to open the door.

One fears for the inhabitants of Falling House. Outside the Hafizhi family home, bulldozers are raking the earth to prepare for a new housing estate. Inside, the jailer has become a one-man wrecking ball, goaded into a fury by the sight of Ensi’s modelling portfolio and doubling down at every turn. First Ensi is imprisoned; then his wife, Zitab (Rina Raminfar); finally his plucky youngest daughter. “This is my prison,” he says. “And I make the rules.”

articles.title: Amelia Dimoldenberg to close doors of Chicken Shop Date
articles.summary: Amelia Dimoldenberg announces she will end her popular YouTube series after more than a decade.
body: Amelia Dimoldenberg has announced she will end Chicken Shop Date after more than a decade.
The presenter, known for her off-the-wall questions and deadpan silences, revealed the news in an Instagram post.
She has become one of the UK's best-known content creators through the web series, which features interviews with rappers, actors and celebrities framed as a "date" with the host.
While "all good dates must come to an end", Dimoldenberg told fans to expect "a few final dates" before the show officially ends.

articles.title: Dolly Parton gets new star on Hollywood Walk of Fame after vandalism
articles.summary: Fans laid flowers on the singer's star after her death, but vandals scratched her name off.
body: Dolly Parton's star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame has been replaced after the original one was vandalised following the late country legend's death last week.
Fans had laid flowers and left candles around her star in the heart of Hollywood, Los Angeles, which was awarded in 1984.
But on Monday, photos showed it had been damaged, external after vandals scratched it, leaving her name badly defaced.
Repairs were carried out on Wednesday, and the Hollywood Historic Trust said, external the new star will be unveiled on Friday.

articles.title: ‘Bucking Fastard’ Review: Kate and Rooney Mara Embrace the Weirdness in Werner Herzog’s Nutty but Thin Tale of Two Sisters Who Behave as One
articles.summary: Orlando Bloom and Domhnall Gleeson also star in this mock-Irish fable about siblings whose hunger for love compels them to tunnel through a mountain.
body: The more intriguing introduction happens shortly after, when Jeanie and Joanie appear as defendants in a court hearing at which their neighbor and former lover daddy, Gareth Mulroney ( Orlando Bloom, adopting a thick and largely convincing Irish accent), has filed for a restraining order. “My cowgirls, they rode me well!” declares the beer-swilling Mulroney, which still titillates the Holbrooke sisters even if they are furious that he married someone else, maintaining that he loves only them.

For as long as we remain in the courtroom, where the judge (Simon Delaney) has made an exception to the standard ruling that only one witness can testify at a time, the oddball movie is frequently funny, and the Maras are a bonkers treat — locking eyes in moments of doubt or snickering conspiratorially when the mood strikes them.
